A proposed approach to material and historical evidence

A mark may be absent because a process never happened, because the mark was damaged later, or because the measuring tool missed it.

Choose an explanation to see what it would need. Weathering, burial and later care can all change which traces survive. A claim about the past needs to account for those changes too.

Choose a reason a trace might be missing. Read what would need checking.

Words used here
preservation
The processes that allow traces to survive, or that change and damage them over time.
Read the fuller explanation

Exposure, burial, salts, disturbance and conservation can change which traces remain available. A missing mark may reflect an absent process, later loss, or a detector that cannot resolve it. Those explanations require different checks.

The material-history programme therefore places preservation between transformation and present observation. An explanation should predict both the proposed working process and the distribution of evidence that could survive it.

Try the record layers on the illustrative stone. The labels are questions for an investigation, not reconstructions of an actual sampled object. Holding that distinction lets curiosity remain generous while claims stay bounded.
